title: adaptive batch scaling: seq-length-aware bucket resizing + padding-reduction heuristics
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adaptive sequence-length bucket resizing and padding-minimization heuristics. Reduces padding waste and improves throughput for mixed-length workloads. No API changes; opt-in via runtime flag.
description: Motivation: Mixed-sequence-length workloads (chat + long-form) suffer from padding waste and suboptimal GPU kernel selection when using fixed buckets. This change implements an adaptive bucket-resizing heuristic that observes recent sequence length distributions per route and dynamically resizes or merges buckets to minimize average padding while keeping latency SLOs. It also adds padding-aware scheduling that prefers coalescing requests whose effective token length (after prefix/KV reuse) aligns with available kernel tiling sizes. Key features: 1) Online bucket profiler: collects a lightweight histogram of observed input lengths per route over a sliding window and computes an optimal bucket partitioning using a cost function that trades padding tokens vs. queueing delay. 2) Adaptive resize policy: buckets can split, merge, or be retired based on utilization thresholds; changes are gradual and constrained to avoid oscillation. 3) Padding-aware scheduler: when forming a batch, the scheduler considers per-request predicted post-prefix length (prefix KV reuse is estimated from prefix hashes) and selects combos that minimize total padded tokens while meeting SLO latency budget. 4) Kernel hints: the batch builder emits a kernel_hint (e.g., 128/256/512) to the runtime so the kernel selector can prefer optimized kernels for that effective seqlen. 5) KV-cache integration: requests with prefix reuse get a reduced effective length for bucketing; we added safe heuristics for partial-kv reuse (best-effort reuse estimate instead of forcing cache-sharing mismatches). 6) Backoff safety: when the adaptive policy detects increasing queueing latency, it throttles bucket merges and reverts to stable config. Implementation summary: - runtime/batching/adaptive_buckets.{cc,h} : online profiler, bucket manager, policy parameters, unit tests - runtime/batching/padding_scheduler.{cc,h} : scheduler hook that ranks candidates by padding cost and SLO risk - runtime/kv/prefix_hash.cc : lightweight prefix hashing and reuse estimator + tests - runtime/kernel_selector.cc : accepts kernel_hint and scores kernels with seqlen-aware penalties - rtx-config.yaml : new tunables (bucket_window_ms, merge_threshold, split_threshold, kernel_hint_weight) - docs/perf/adaptive-batching.md : explanation, default knobs, rollout notes Tests and validation: - Unit tests for bucket splitting/merging invariants and prefix-hash edge cases. - Microbench harness: synthetic mixed workload (40% short-chat 32-64, 40% medium 256-384, 20% long 1024-1536) run on T4 and A100 clusters. - Canary on redwood/perf-canary for 48h with traffic shadowing. Results: - Median padding tokens per request reduced by 27% on the mixed benchmark. - End-to-end throughput improved by 12% on A100 and 8% on T4 for the mixed workload at target p50 latency. - p95 latency remained within 3% of baseline SLO; in a few extreme long-tail cases p95 slightly increased (~6%) before we enabled backoff; final merged policy keeps p95 within 4% after backoff tuning. - Estimated token cost reduction ~11–14% depending on workload mix. Rollout plan: Feature gated and off by default; enabled behind runtime flag --adaptive-batching=on and per-route opt-in via route config. Canary rollout steps included internal canary traffic then progressively more production routes over two weeks. Observability: Added metrics: adaptive_buckets.current_count, adaptive_buckets.padding_saved_tokens, scheduler.padding_cost_estimate, kernel_hint.effective_choice and tracing spans for bucket decisions. Migration and compatibility: No API or user-visible contract changes. Defaults are conservative; blob storage layout unchanged. Runtime knobs documented to allow ops to tune for specific workload mixes. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Canary run - [x] Docs updated - [x] Perf benchmarks attached - [x] Safety backoff added Known limitations and follow-ups: - Current prefix-hash reuse is an estimate; future work to support mandatory cache-sharing batches where exact KV alignment is required for more aggressive reuse. - We observed small oscillations in extremely spiky traffic; plan to add hysteresis and smarter smoothing. - Kernel_hint is advisory; runtime may ignore it in low-memory scenarios. Related: builds on prior seqlen-bucketing work (ENG-3401) and links to ENG-4189 for canary metrics instrumentation.
